source.author: verg
source.text: Sin autem ad pugnam exierint, nam saepe duobus regibus incessit magno discordia motu, continuoque animos vulgi et trepidantia bello corda licet longe praesciscere; namque morantes Martius ille aeris rauci canor increpat et vox auditur fractos sonitus imitata tubarum; tum trepidae inter se coeunt pennisque coruscant spiculaque exacuunt rostris aptantque lacertos et circa regem atque ipsa ad praetoria densae miscentur magnisque vocant clamoribus hostem.
source.text_original: Sin autem ad pugnam exierint, nam saepe duobus / regibus incessit magno discordia motu, / continuoque animos vulgi et trepidantia bello / corda licet longe praesciscere; namque morantes / Martius ille aeris rauci canor increpat et vox / auditur fractos sonitus imitata tubarum; / tum trepidae inter se coeunt pennisque coruscant / spiculaque exacuunt rostris aptantque lacertos / et circa regem atque ipsa ad praetoria densae / miscentur magnisque vocant clamoribus hostem.
source.text_english: But if they have gone out to battle—for often great discord has arisen between two kings with violent upheaval—you may at once foresee from afar the spirits of the crowd and the hearts trembling for war; for while they delay, that martial din of harsh bronze rebukes them, and a voice is heard imitating the broken sounds of trumpets; then, in their fear, they gather together, flash with their wings, sharpen their spear-points and fit them to their beaks, and about the king and even around the headquarters themselves they crowd in dense ranks, and with great cries they summon the enemy.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: si multi sint in examine apum reges, peribunt aut dissipabuntur, dum regibus incessit magno discordia motu; si plures in armento duces, tam diu proeliabuntur, donec unus optineat; si multi in exercitu inperatores, nec pareri poterit a milite, cum diuersa iubeantur, nec ab iis ipsis unitas optineri, cum sibi quisque pro moribus consulat.
reuse.text_original: si multi sint in examine apum reges, peribunt aut dissipabuntur, dum regibus incessit magno discordia motu; si plures in armento duces, tam diu proeliabuntur, donec unus optineat; si multi in exercitu inperatores, nec pareri poterit a milite, cum diuersa iubeantur, nec ab iis ipsis unitas optineri, cum sibi quisque pro moribus consulat.
reuse.text_english: If there are many kings in a swarm of bees, they will perish or be scattered, when discord has arisen among the kings with great disturbance; if there are several leaders in a herd, they will fight for so long until one prevails; if there are many commanders in an army, neither will the soldier be able to obey, since different orders are given, nor will unity be maintained by those men themselves, since each one will act according to his own habits.
